pages.text: A swan took off her necklace and left it on the porch. "Stay here while I take a bath." Its glass beads sparkled in the sunlight.
"I'll take it to your room!" Kota scooped it up in one paw and ran. The beads dangled and swung precariously.
Kota tripped at the threshold. The necklace flew! Dad slid forward and caught it. Kota's heart gave a jolt.
Dad held out the necklace. "Precious things need a special way of carrying. Shall we play Handle with Care?" Kota swallowed hard.
"Can you make a bowl with both paws?" Kota cupped them together. Dad gently laid the necklace inside.
In the paw-bowl, the beads settled down. Kota walked slowly, step by step. The beads sparkled without swinging.
Gently onto the cabinet in the swan's room—there! "Not a single wobble!" Kota spread their empty paws wide, tail rising.
When the swan returned, she smiled at her necklace. "The beads seem brighter. Is it because they traveled with such care?" Kota's cheeks glowed like the beads.
Now Kota counted before carrying anyone's belongings. "One, a bowl of two paws! Two, gently! Three, slowly!" Precious things liked Kota's paws.
Dad held Kota carefully in both arms that evening. "Two paws know how to treasure something." "Two paws, handle with care!" Kota cupped Dad's face.
